question: High heels weren't invented for fashion. They began as practical footwear for men doing which activity?
source_excerpt: traces their history to Persian men in the 10th century, who wore heels while on horseback so their feet would fit better in the stirrups

extra.why_interesting: Players picture heels as a women's fashion item made for looks. The truth is that they began as practical gear for male soldiers on horseback, and a player who thinks about what a heel could catch on can work it out.
extra.verification_notes: Bata Shoe Museum curator Semmelhack traces heels to 10th-century Persian horse riders using them to hold the foot in stirrups (https://www.today.com/today/amp/tdna100969).

explanation: Persian cavalrymen wore heels so their feet would stay locked in the stirrups while they stood up to shoot arrows. European noblemen later copied the look, and only after that did heels become a women's fashion.
